title: Per-customer IaC flavoring and overlay design for private VPC deployments
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: recommend and implement a reproducible pattern for per-customer Terraform customizations ("flavors"/overlays/variable layers) that works with our Private (VPC) offering and supports safe upgrades and health checks. This ticket captures a proposed reference implementation, rationale, migration plan for a couple of pilot customers, and CI/CD guardrails.

Why: current customer customizations are ad-hoc (customer-specific branches, local patches, or large variable files). This causes drift, difficult upgrades, and slow incident remediation. We need a pattern that: (1) keeps a single upstream core module for Redwood, (2) lets operations/SEs produce small, auditable per-customer overlay packages, and (3) supports automated upgrade hooks and health validation post-upgrade.

Scope: design the module composition (core + tenant-wrapper + override-layer), variable precedence rules, example repo layout for customers, CI pipeline changes for plan-only & guarded applies, runtime healthcheck integration (Terraform -> Orch -> health test), and docs + migration checklist for 2 pilot customers (ACME Corp, FinNova).

Non-goals: full multi-tenant runtime changes, provisioning new hardware types, or replacing existing customer-specific IaC entirely in one sweep.
acceptance_criteria: Deliver a reference repo with: core modules, a customer wrapper module, and a documented overlay pattern
CI pipeline templates that do plan-only for overlays and gated applies after automated post-plan checks
Upgrade hooks implemented as optional lifecycle modules and an example healthcheck job that runs after apply
Migration guide for two pilots and runbook for rollback if healthchecks fail
Security review notes documented for IAM/KMS overrides
tasks: Design module composition: core modules (networking, compute, storage, secrets) + tenant-wrapper + overlay/patch module
Draft variable precedence rules and naming conventions (e.g., rdc_core_, rdc_customer_, override files)
Create reference repo: infra/customer-flavors-template with examples for ACME and FinNova
Add Terragrunt/Makefile examples for local dev + CI integration
Implement post-apply healthcheck choreography using terraform null_resource + external script (orchestration job)
Add plan gating to CI: automated drift detection + human approval thresholds
Run pilot migration for ACME: port existing vars into overlay and run dry-run
Document rollback process and pre/post upgrade validation checklist
progress_updates: 2025-01-14: Brainstormed patterns with Infra and SEs — consensus on core + wrapper + overlay model. Key constraint: overlays must be small & composable.
2025-01-21: Prototype repo initialized (infra/customer-flavors-template) with core networking and example customer-overlay for ACME. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1842
2025-01-28: Ran workshop with Solutions Engineering; noted two customer constraints: customer-managed KMS vs Redwood-managed KMS, and custom subnets for compliance. Added variable knobs for both.

2025-02-04: Implemented a terraform null_resource + local-exec health script that calls runtime health endpoint and checks KV cache priming. Health script repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-healthchecks/tree/eng-20321

2025-02-10: CI gating prototype created in GitHub Actions: plan -> automated static checks -> run healthcheck against staging -> if failures, fail the gated apply. Pipeline PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1899
review_feedback: PM (Jin Li): prefer clearer separation of customer secrets — avoid allowing customers to override KMS keys without explicit approval.
Security (Lena Ortiz): require explicit security_review_required flag for overlays that change IAM policies. Suggested adding a signed-change policy for apply steps.
Design (Ravi Singh): requested an example of overlay that only changes tags and monitoring settings to show minimal customization surface.
Infra lead (Daniel Cho): recommended using small patch modules (apply-as-resources) rather than large variable maps to reduce merge conflict risk during upgrades.
open_questions: Should overlays be distributed as separate repos per customer or as directories within a single customer-repo? Trade-offs for compliance/legal audits?
How do we prevent sensitive variables from being accidentally committed in overlay directories? (suggested: git hooks + pre-commit + secret-scanning policy)
Do we allow customers to inject arbitrary providers (e.g., custom kms provider) or only expose restricted knobs?
next_steps: Finish CI gating changes and merge pipeline PR into infra/main
Execute pilot migration for ACME (schedule Feb 24) and run full upgrade test including simulated failure and rollback
Create customer-facing migration checklist and book a runbook handoff with Solutions Engineering
Coordinate security review and finalize required signoff checklist
